title: Zariski logification and characteristic geometry
statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $X$ [pqf-def-locnoeth] and Zariski prelog sheaf $P$ [def-trf-zariski-log-structure], construct a Zariski log structure $Z$ with a normalized unit-pushout presentation $z$, and a monoid sheaf $K$ with a characteristic quotient presentation $k$ [def-trf-prelog-logification-data]. Then $z$ is universal for structurally compatible maps from $P$ to Zariski log structures. At every $x$, the stalk of $Z$ is the pushout of $P_x$ and $O_x^\times$ over the inverse unit submonoid, normalized on all pair germs and on the canonical ring-unit inclusion. The stalk of $K$ is the Associates quotient of this pushout, normalized by $k$ on pair germs. Both presentations restrict to every slice with exactly the restricted maps. This statement concerns only the Zariski site.

proof.text: Form the sectionwise congruence quotient of P(U) times O(U) units. Restrictions preserve its generators. Sheafify in monoids by [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification]. The structure map extends uniquely to O. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], locally a section is [p,a]; if its structural image is invertible, beta(p) is invertible and the relation makes this [1,beta(p)a]. Local equality glues, showing the log axiom on sheaves and then on stalks.

proof.text: A compatible map to a Zariski log structure K extends by [p,a] mapping to f(p)j_K(a). This respects all generators because structural maps preserve the unique lifts of units. Sheafification gives existence and equality on pairs gives uniqueness. This is the Zariski universal property.

proof.text: Sheafification preserves open stalks by local lifting and shrinking equalities. Apply [lem-trf-filtered-varying-prelog-pushout] to the open-neighborhood diagram. Its normalized pair formula is the required stalk isomorphism; the formula on units follows from the log unit bijection.

source.place: ILO VIII, opening of section 3, p.97, and 3.3.2, p.106; arbitrary-prelog formulation and detailed proof expanded by the agent from the parent node.

proof.text: Sheafify the sectionwise quotient by monoid units. A unit germ and its inverse can be represented on one neighborhood, with the inverse equations after shrinking; [lem-trf-filtered-ring-log-pushout] and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] give the same finite-stage argument. Hence quotienting by units commutes with stalks, and the preceding stalk isomorphism gives the characteristic formula on pairs.
